term: stipulated complete input and response law
definition: History separately stores a Boolean law selector, prior preference and imposed constraint. input includes both preference and imposed constraint. response forces true when constrained; otherwise law false follows preference and law true reverses it. action is that response applied to the recorded law and input. The input is complete only for this defined table; it is not claimed to encode the complete physical past.
note: Analyst-defined control motivated by the Carneades definition fork; no source attribution. Adequacy and applicability remain open. See docs/notes/carneades-choice-context.md.
